Subject: Retainer payment pending — VAT IDs and split entities

Hi Nikhil,

We’re ready to release the initial retainer for the consulting engagement (PO attached), but our payments team hit a snag with the invoice that Redwood issued. HelioCorp will be paying the retainer from two legal entities:

- HelioCorp Europe GmbH (DE) — VAT: DE123456789
- HelioCorp UK Ltd — VAT: GB987654321

Our AP needs one of two paths confirmed before we can process payment:

1) Issue two separate invoices (one to the German entity with reverse-charge net amount, and one to the UK entity with VAT charged if applicable), or
2) Issue a single invoice split by line item that clearly shows entity allocations, VAT treatment, and billing addresses.

Because the German entity is claiming the reverse-charge mechanism, our tax team is also asking for Redwood’s VAT registration status in the EU and a confirmation that reverse-charge is appropriate for the service type (software integration / SaaS professional services).

We’d like to avoid payment being stuck in AP suspense. If Redwood prefers to have funds held in a short-term escrow until VAT evidence is validated, we can arrange that, but we need the paperwork to match our payment routing.

Attached: PO and a spreadsheet with the entity details.

Can you confirm how Redwood wants to proceed and provide any supporting VAT documentation?

Thanks,

Jane Carter

Subject: Re: Retainer payment pending — VAT IDs and split entities

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear note and the PO.

Short answer: we can do either (1) two invoices or (2) a single split invoice. From a tax-compliance perspective the cleanest is two invoices tied to each legal entity — one showing net-of-VAT with a reverse-charge reference (for HelioCorp Europe GmbH) and one showing whatever UK VAT treatment applies for the UK entity. That approach avoids cross-entity allocation ambiguity on both sides.

A few practical items we need to confirm:
- Please confirm the billing addresses you want on each invoice and the registered company names to match your legal entities.
- We need a copy of both entities’ VAT certificates or a VIES check result (screenshot or registry lookup) to retain in our files.
- For the EU reverse charge, we’ll include the tax note: "Reverse charge — customer liable for VAT under Article 194, EU VAT Directive / B2B supplies" plus the other mandated line items.
- If you prefer escrow, please provide the escrow agent details and proposed release conditions; we can coordinate with Finance.

I’ve attached a draft pro forma showing the two-invoice option and a recommended short note to include on the German invoice. If you’re happy with that, Marissa will issue the official proformas from Billing and we’ll follow up with the final signed invoice.

Quick ask to our internal team: Marissa / Rishi — can we confirm whether issuing two invoices requires any cross-entity billing code changes on our side or an intercompany memo? Rishi, do we need to notify tax or bookings?

Thanks — I’ll await the VAT evidence and address confirmations.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping. Operational notes from Billing/Finance:

- We can issue two invoices to two separate legal entities. Operationally we will route them to two billing entities in NetSuite (Redwood EU LTD for the reverse-charge net invoice; Redwood UK Services for the UK-facing invoice). That routing already exists for customers with multi-entity billing.
- Rishi — from a revenue recognition / tax registration perspective, do we need any new VAT registration in Germany if we are only issuing a net reverse-charge invoice to an EU customer? My read is no, provided the supply is B2B and the customer provides a valid VAT ID. Please confirm.
- Assuming VAT evidence is provided (VIES check screenshot or certificate), we’ll set the German invoice to net with the reverse-charge annotation and attach the evidence to the invoice record.
- For the UK invoice: we need to check whether the supply is VATable under UK rules; if so, we will charge VAT at the appropriate rate and apply the standard remittance schedule.

Action items:
- Nikhil: confirm the exact billing names/addresses to print.
- Jane: please upload the VAT evidence (or confirm the VIES URLs) and indicate whether you want two PDFs or a combined statement.
- Rishi: confirm any tax registration or booking impacts.

If there’s any risk of payment delay, we should offer the escrow option to HelioCorp but note this will delay revenue recognition until released.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
